Synopsis:
    The Indian rupee is extending its weekly decline driven by a sharp oil price rally (Brent up ~12% on the week, nearing $110/bbl) fuelled by escalating Middle East shipping route attacks. Rising U.S. Treasury yields (~5% on 10-year), driven by stronger-than-expected PPI data and ~70% market-priced probability of a Fed rate hike, are compounding rupee weakness. The RBI is increasingly stepping back from defending the currency, as sustained oil import costs threaten India's external balances, growth and inflation outlook. Asian equities and currencies are broadly lower.
